cards.front: Recall a key point about Material Removal Processes
cards.back: Material removal (subtractive) processes cut material away from a workpiece to create the desired shape.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Material Removal Processes
cards.back: Sawing and shearing are basic cutting methods: sawing uses a toothed blade; shearing cuts sheet metal between two blades.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Material Removal Processes
cards.back: Laser cutting uses a focused CO2 or fibre laser to melt, burn or vaporise material; highly accurate and capable of complex profiles.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Material Removal Processes
cards.back: Turning produces cylindrical shapes on a lathe: the workpiece rotates and a single-point cutting tool moves along it.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Material Removal Processes
cards.back: Milling uses a rotating multi-tooth cutter to produce flat surfaces, slots, pockets and complex 3D profiles.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Material Removal Processes
cards.back: Drilling creates round holes using a rotating drill bit; pillar drills and lathe tailstocks are common setups.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Material Removal Processes
cards.back: Spindle speed (RPM) = (Cutting speed x 1000) / (pi x Diameter); always calculate for the workpiece or cutter diameter.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Material Removal Processes
cards.back: Feed rate affects surface finish and tool life: too fast causes poor finish; too slow causes rubbing and work hardening.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Material Removal Processes
cards.back: Chemical etching removes material using acid or ferric chloride; the standard method for PCB manufacture.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Material Removal Processes
cards.back: CNC (Computer Numerical Control) machines automate turning, milling and laser cutting for precision and repeatability.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Material Removal Processes
cards.back: Coolant/lubricant reduces friction, removes heat and improves surface finish in machining operations.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Material Removal Processes
cards.back: Tolerances achievable: turning/milling typically +/-0.05 mm; grinding +/-0.01 mm; laser cutting +/-0.1 mm.

cards.back: 1. For Material Removal Processes questions, use precise design and technology terminology 2. Consider function, aesthetics, ergonomics, sustainability and cost in your answers 3.
